newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine five-year note coupon at 14.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine five-year note coupon at 14.5 pct.

text.p: The coupon rate on the Philippines' five-year fixed rate Treasury note slipped to 14.5 percent on Tuesday from 15 percent at the previous auction held last August, the Bureau of Treasury said.
The average rate fell to 14.423 percent from 14.927, with the low at 13.875 and the high at 14.5 percent.
The auction generated bids worth 6.720 billion pesos, of which 2.0 billion pesos were awarded.
Dealers said the auction fetched a lower-than-expected rate due to demand from foreign investors. Some had expected the coupon rate to be at 14.6 to 14.7 percent.
"Everybody was saying the five-year notes were already trading at 14.6 to 14.7 percent as of yesterday," a big bank dealer said.
Moreover, institutions had bid to get the five-year notes to replace maturing floating rate Treasury notes next week, dealers said. - Manila newsroom (632) 841-8937
